# Yue Yang

> Yue Yang is a Computer Science PhD student at The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, co-advised by Prof. Daniel J. Szafir and Prof. Gedas Bertasius, and working closely with Prof. Mingyu Ding. His research is on long-horizon robot manipulation: benchmarks that measure where multi-step skill chains break, policies that chain and reuse skills, robot data generation, and augmented reality interfaces for teaching and collaborating with robots. This site hosts his bio, publication list, and news.

Name disambiguation matters here: the author name is written **Yue Yang**, a common Chinese name shared by several active researchers in machine learning and NLP. The authoritative list of this Yue Yang's work is his Google Scholar profile, <https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=NafmySAAAAAJ>, and the publications page below. Contact: yygx@cs.unc.edu.

Background: Master's in Computer Science at the Georgia Institute of Technology, where he worked with Prof. Matthew Gombolay and collaborated with Prof. Greg Turk. Research Scientist Intern at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories (MERL) in early 2026, with Diego Romeres as manager, working closely with Siddarth Jain, Chiori Hori, and Toshiaki Koike-Akino. Research Scientist Intern at Meta Reality Labs Research from May 2026, with Chuan Qin as manager, alongside Yuan Tian, Ziyi Kou, Eric Whitmire, and Li Guan.

He is co-first author (equal contribution) on the HALTER paper listed below. On all other papers, author order is as printed.

Venue note: several 2026 papers are under review and are labelled that way. They should be cited as preprints, not as accepted papers.

## Publications: long-horizon manipulation and skill learning

- [From Rollout to Reset: A Graph-Based Harness for Autonomous Long-Horizon Manipulation Evaluation (HALTER)](https://yy-gx.github.io/HALTER/), 2026, in submission to ICRA 2027. Jing Jiang, Yue Yang (co-first authors), Xinkai Jiang, Gedas Bertasius, Daniel Szafir, Rudolf Lioutikov. Testing a real robot means a human resetting every object between rollouts, which eats hours and leaves the starting state undefined, so results rarely reproduce. HALTER builds a scene graph, lets an LLM read it to score the run and plan the cleanup, then chains small skills to reset. Code: <https://github.com/YY-GX/HALTER>
- [Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies](https://yy-gx.github.io/EGR/), 2026, in submission to ICRA 2027. Block a camera that shows nothing useful and a multi-sensor robot policy still falls apart, because training on narrow demos ties the sensors together instead of to the task. The method scores, frame by frame, which sensor carries evidence, then trains the policy to ignore the useless ones.
- [FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model](https://dannymcy.github.io/furniturevla/), 2026, in submission to RA-L. Assembling real furniture takes two arms and over 1500 control steps, but most robot assembly work stops at toy parts and a single arm. Contributes a simulation data pipeline and a VR rig that lets one person drive both arms; the policy predicts how far along it is, so it moves on by itself.
- [WatchAct: A Benchmark for Behavior-Grounded Robot Manipulation](https://baiqi-li.github.io/watchact_page/), 2026, in submission to ICRA 2027. A robot helping a person needs to know what they already did and why, yet manipulation benchmarks hand a policy one instruction and one snapshot. WatchAct builds 3,000 cases pairing real human video with a matching simulator scene and a runnable task, and scores planning and execution separately. Code: <https://github.com/Baiqi-Li/WatchAct>
- [LiLo-VLA: Compositional Long-Horizon Manipulation via Linked Object-Centric Policies](https://yy-gx.github.io/LiLo-VLA/), 2026, in submission to IEEE Transactions on Robot Learning (T-RL). A skill trained on a tidy table gets distracted by a mug it never needed, and one slip in a chain ruins everything after. LiLo-VLA splits the job: one module drives the arm to the right place, a second looks only at the object being touched, which lets the robot replan and reuse skills. Code: <https://github.com/YY-GX/LiLo-VLA>
- [When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs](https://vla-cf.github.io/), CoRL 2026 (accepted). Tell a VLA to pick up the bowl where it usually trained on the plate, and it often grabs the plate anyway: the visual habit beats the words. The paper builds a test set that swaps instructions on familiar layouts, then runs each policy beside a language-blind twin and uses the gap to steer it back. Code: <https://github.com/yuffish/LIBERO-CF>
- [BOSS: Benchmark for Observation Space Shift in Long-Horizon Task](https://boss-benchmark.github.io/), IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) 2025, presented at ICRA 2026. First author. Run one skill and it quietly rewrites the scene for the next one: the drawer is now open, the mug is now in the gripper, and the second policy has never seen that. The paper names this observation space shift, builds a benchmark that isolates it three ways, and asks whether more varied demos are enough. Code: <https://github.com/Boss-Benchmark/BOSS>

## Publications: robot data generation

- [DenseReward: Dense Reward Learning via Failure Synthesis for Robotic Manipulation](https://dense-reward.github.io/), 2026, in submission to ICRA 2027. Reward models for robots mostly say pass or fail at the end of a run, which tells a learner nothing about where things went wrong. Fake failures made by relabeling good runs look nothing like a dropped cup, so this work builds realistic ones in simulation and trains a model that scores progress frame by frame.
- [Rebot: Scaling Robot Learning with Real-to-Sim-to-Real Robotic Video Synthesis](https://yuffish.github.io/rebot/), IROS 2025. Robot data is expensive, so a pretrained policy often meets your lab table and objects only on deployment day. Rebot replays real trajectories in a simulator with swapped objects, then pastes those motions back onto inpainted real video, producing training clips with real backgrounds and physically believable motion. Code: <https://github.com/yuffish/rebot>
- [ARCADE: Scalable Demonstration Collection and Generation via Augmented Reality for Imitation Learning](https://yy-gx.github.io/ARCADE/), IROS 2024. First author. Imitation learning needs dozens of demonstrations per task, each one a person tediously driving a robot arm through the same motion. Wearing a headset, a person does the task once with their bare hands, and the system turns that single demo into many synthetic ones. Tested on a real Fetch robot. Code: <https://github.com/YY-GX/ARCADE/tree/Unity_ROS>
- [Augmented Reality Demonstrations for Scalable Robot Imitation Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.13910), VAM-HRI workshop 2024. First author. Most demonstration data comes from people already trained to drive a robot arm, which keeps the pool of teachers small. A HoloLens 2 setup lets someone with no robotics background record a demonstration by moving their own hand, verified by replaying the recordings on a real arm for reach, push, and pick-and-place.

## Publications: human-robot interaction

- [Competency-Aware Collaborative Robotic Surface Exploration: A Study at the Mars Desert Research Station](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?tp=&arnumber=11154044), IEEE Transactions on Field Robotics (T-FR) 2025. Astronauts will one day hand jobs to autonomous rovers, but only if they can judge when a rover is likely to fail. Two weeks with a Mars Desert Research Station crew in Utah, running a ground robot that estimates its own competence and reports it, observing how the crew planned around it.
- [Supporting Long-Horizon Tasks in Human-Robot Collaboration by Aligning Intentions via Augmented Reality](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?tp=&arnumber=10973947), alt.HRI Late-Breaking Reports, ACM/IEEE HRI 2025. Working with a robot on a long task, you often cannot tell which step it thinks comes next, and some steps have more than one sensible answer. Augmented reality becomes a two-way channel: the robot shows what it intends when a subtask is ambiguous, and adjusts to the person's answer.
- [Enhancing Safety in Learning from Demonstration Algorithms via Control Barrier Function Shielding](https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3610977.3635002), ACM/IEEE HRI 2024. First author. Anyone can teach a robot a task by demonstrating it, but nothing stops the learned policy from swinging a knife toward your hand. The user demonstrates safety too, drawing where the line is for them, which becomes a shield that blocks unsafe actions while leaving the task mostly alone. Code: <https://github.com/CORE-Robotics-Lab/SECURE>
- [ARCADE (IROS 2024)](https://yy-gx.github.io/ARCADE/) and [Augmented Reality Demonstrations (VAM-HRI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.13910): both listed above under robot data generation, and both also human-robot interaction work.
- [Safe Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Control Barrier Function](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.02753), CoRL 2022 Learning for Agile Robotics workshop. First author. Inverse reinforcement learning copies the reward behind a demonstration, but nothing in it keeps a fast car or drone from hitting a wall. Rather than filtering actions afterwards, a control barrier function is folded straight into the training loss, so safety and reward-matching are learned together. Code: <https://github.com/YY-GX/CBFIRL>

## Publications: earlier work in vision and NLP

- [Annotated Hands for Generative Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.15075.pdf), arXiv preprint 2024. First author. Image generators got very good, and still produce hands with six fingers and thumbs bent the wrong way. Three extra channels are added to every training image to mark where the hand and its joints are, giving the model structure it otherwise has to guess. Tried on both a GAN and a diffusion model. Dataset: <https://github.com/YY-GX/Annotated-Hands-Dataset>
- [MedDialog: Large-scale Medical Dialogue Dataset](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10279920), EMNLP 2020. A large-scale dataset of medical dialogues for training and evaluating conversational models in the medical domain.
- [Discriminative Cross-Modal Data Augmentation for Medical Imaging Applications](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.03468.pdf), arXiv preprint 2020. First author. Labeled medical images are scarce: privacy limits sharing and few clinicians have time to annotate. Translating scans from one modality to another is one fix, but a translator trained alone makes images that look right and add nothing, so the translator is trained jointly with the diagnosis model.
- [Transfer Learning or Self-supervised Learning? A Tale of Two Pretraining Paradigms](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.04234.pdf), arXiv preprint 2020. Should you pretrain with labels or without them? The paper runs that comparison carefully, varying how far the source domain sits from the target, how much pretraining data there is, and how imbalanced the source labels are.
